security_audit.summary: All 95 static findings are false positives involving documentation examples, explicitly discouraged patterns, or legitimate audit references. No evidence found of prompt injection, credential theft, or malicious execution. Two semantic findings identify security guidance errors concerning Permissions-Policy delivery and structuredClone behavior.

remediation.issue: Permissions-Policy meta tags do not enforce the documented feature restrictions.
remediation.suggestion: Replace the meta examples with Permissions-Policy HTTP response headers using valid syntax. Verify deployed headers and feature restrictions in a browser.

remediation.issue: The structuredClone example incorrectly claims that cloning removes __proto__ keys and functions.
remediation.suggestion: Explain that structuredClone preserves __proto__ data keys and throws on functions. Validate keys recursively before merges and test prototype-pollution defenses.

semantic_findings.title: Permissions Policy Examples Do Not Enforce Restrictions
semantic_findings.description: The skill recommends meta http-equiv="Permissions-Policy" to restrict geolocation, camera, and microphone. Browsers require the HTTP response header, so copied examples leave these policy restrictions unenforced.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Both examples use an unsupported meta delivery mechanism. This creates false assurance about feature restrictions, although browser permission prompts still apply.

semantic_findings.title: Cloning Is Incorrectly Presented as Dangerous-Key Sanitization
semantic_findings.description: The reference states that structuredClone drops __proto__ and functions, then labels its result deepSafe. Cloning preserves __proto__ data keys, so later unsafe merges can still expose prototype-pollution risks.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: A local runtime check confirmed that structuredClone preserves an own __proto__ key and throws DataCloneError for functions. Cloning alone does not sanitize merge inputs.

content.user_title: Improve Web Security and Code Quality
content.value_statement: Web applications can accumulate insecure settings, deprecated APIs, and browser compatibility problems. This skill guides evidence-based reviews and targeted fixes using Lighthouse, source inspection, and security checks.
actual_capabilities: Guide live Lighthouse Best Practices audits when compatible browser tools are available, with a CLI fallback.
Review HTTPS, mixed content, CSP, Trusted Types, security headers, and third-party script integrity.
Identify deprecated browser APIs and recommend feature detection, asynchronous requests, and controlled polyfill delivery.
Review error handling, React error boundaries, source-map exposure, and event-listener cleanup.
Check HTML structure, semantic elements, image proportions, and contextual permission requests.
Guide dependency checks and repeat audits after targeted changes.
limitations: Requires external tools and access to the application for live audits; the skill does not bundle an audit engine.
Lighthouse scores do not establish application security or replace comprehensive security testing.
Permissions-Policy meta examples and structuredClone sanitization claims require correction before reuse.
Framework behavior, browser support, and dependency vulnerabilities require verification against the actual project versions.

use_cases.title: Modernize a Frontend Application
use_cases.description: Review deprecated APIs, feature detection, resource loading, and listener cleanup before updating an existing interface.

use_cases.title: Review Deployment Security
use_cases.description: Compare deployed headers, third-party script integrity, dependency findings, and source-map access against the security checklist.

use_cases.title: Verify Release Quality
use_cases.description: Collect Lighthouse evidence, investigate console failures, check HTML validity, and compare results after fixes.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Page
prompt_templates.prompt: Review [page or file] for web development best practices. Identify the three most important issues and explain each proposed correction.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of a single page.

prompt_templates.title: Modernize Browser Code
prompt_templates.prompt: Review [component] for deprecated APIs, browser detection, blocking requests, and listener leaks. Propose focused changes for [supported browsers] and relevant tests.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate maintenance of an existing component.

prompt_templates.title: Check Deployed Security
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit [authorized application URL] for HTTPS, response headers, CSP, third-party integrity, and source-map exposure. Cite runtime evidence and separate verified issues from assumptions.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced security review of an authorized deployment.

prompt_templates.title: Fix and Verify Findings
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit [authorized application] using available Lighthouse tools and focused source checks. Prioritize evidenced findings, apply scoped fixes, and rerun checks to verify changes.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced audit and remediation with repository and runtime access.

output_examples.input: Review a page with synchronous requests and event listeners that remain active after navigation.
output: Finding: Synchronous requests block the main thread. Replace them with asynchronous requests and explicit failure handling.
Finding: Listeners remain active after navigation. Remove them during cleanup or attach an AbortController.
Verification: Repeat navigation and confirm listener cleanup and responsive interactions.

output_examples.input: Review a deployment that publishes source maps and lacks security response headers.
output: Finding: Public source maps may expose original source. Restrict access and remove embedded source content from uploaded maps.
Recommendation: Configure appropriate security response headers and test CSP in report-only mode before enforcement.
Verification: Inspect deployed responses and repeat the same audit. Do not treat a high Lighthouse score as security assurance.

best_practices: Combine runtime evidence with source, dependency, and deployment configuration checks before reporting a finding.
Apply focused fixes, test behavior, and repeat the same audit to verify improvements.
Verify browser security mechanisms and sanitization behavior before copying examples into production.
anti_patterns: Treating a high Lighthouse score as proof that an application is secure.
Copying placeholder security policies or illustrative snippets into production without validating their behavior.
Running external scans or submitting private application data without authorization.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The marketplace lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code. Available audit integrations depend on the host environment.

faq.question: Does the skill include Lighthouse?
faq.answer: No. It guides compatible live Lighthouse tools when available and recommends the Lighthouse CLI as a fallback.

faq.question: Can it review code without a running page?
faq.answer: Yes. It can guide source and configuration review, but deployed headers and runtime behavior require separate verification.

faq.question: Does a passing audit guarantee security?
faq.answer: No. Lighthouse and checklist reviews do not replace comprehensive security testing or application-specific threat analysis.

faq.question: Are all examples ready for production?
faq.answer: No. Correct the Permissions-Policy meta examples and structuredClone sanitization claim. Verify all policies, placeholders, and dependencies before reuse.

faq.question: What areas does the skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers web security settings, browser compatibility, deprecated APIs, error handling, source maps, HTML quality, event cleanup, and permission requests.
